content.title: KITCHEN FIXES FOR ANNOYING LITTLE PROBLEMS YOUR {{MEDICINE CABINET}} DOESN'T HAVE
facts: **Hiccups** – Swallow 1 tsp of dry sugar to reset the nerve signal.
**Burnt Tongue** – Press a spoon of plain yogurt on it to cool and soothe.
**Bug Bite Itch** – Dab on a paste of baking soda and water for quick relief.
**Nosebleed** – Pinch the soft part of your nose and lean forward for 10 minutes.
**Sore Throat** – Gargle warm salt water (1/2 tsp salt per cup) 3x/day.
**Hangnail Pain** – Soak the finger in warm olive oil for 5 minutes to soften skin.
**Bad Breath After Onions** – Chew on fresh parsley or mint leaves to neutralize odor.
**Leg Cramp at Night** – Pull your toes toward your shin and hold for 30 seconds.
**Splinter Removal** – Soak the area in warm water with Epsom salt to draw it out.
**Chapped Lips** – Rub a thin layer of coconut oil before bed to lock in moisture.
**Follow along** – for more quick fixes like this you can actually use today.
content.caption:
A few of these deserve a bit more explanation. The sugar trick for hiccups works because the granules briefly irritate the vagus nerve, interrupting the spasm signal that's causing the diaphragm to jump. Salt water gargles for a sore throat pull excess fluid out of inflamed tissue through osmosis, which is why the swelling and scratchiness ease up so fast. And that Epsom salt soak for a splinter isn't just softening the skin — the magnesium sulfate helps reduce local swelling around the splinter, making it easier for your body (or tweezers) to push it out. Everyone's body reacts a little differently, so listen to yours and adjust as needed.
